editorial:
If you love a good survival horror flick, Wrong Turn (2021) might be right up your alley. The story follows Jen and her group of friends as they head out to hike the Appalachian Trail. They ignore warnings to stay on the path and wander off course, stumbling into land owned by The Foundation, a hidden community of mountain dwellers who will do anything to protect their way of life. The vibe is tense and unsettling from the start, with a creepy backwoods atmosphere that keeps you on edge. The characters feel real enough, and you actually care about what happens to them, which makes the danger feel more personal.

The acting is solid across the board, and the pacing keeps things moving without dragging. The action scenes are brutal and well-staged, and the movie does a good job building dread before things go sideways. On the downside, some plot twists feel a bit forced, and a few characters make frustrating decisions. Still, if you enjoy survival horror with a twist, this one delivers.
endingExplained: In the final act, Jen is captured by The Foundation and forced to marry their leader. She plays along to survive, but secretly plans her escape. During a ceremony, she fights back and kills several members. She escapes into the woods with her boyfriend, but The Foundation tracks them down. In the last scene, Jen returns months later with a gun and shoots the leader, revealing she has been planning revenge all along. The twist shows she was never truly broken.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves survival horror with a dark twist.
